subject: Request to change invoice payee & tax handling for PO 4321
messages:
From: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@cleardock.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: payments@cleardock.com
Date: Fri, 29 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request to change invoice payee & tax handling for PO 4321

Hi Marcus,

Quick one from our procurement/tax teams. Attached is PO 4321 for the upcoming onboarding. Our tax group is asking that invoices be issued to our EU entity (Cleardock Europe OU) instead of the US parent, and that Redwood apply a reverse-charge (VAT) treatment rather than charging VAT on the invoice. This helps our AP process and avoids a local VAT reclaim.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can change the invoice payee on this order and apply reverse-charge? If this requires an amendment to the Order Form or a specific billing entity mapping, please outline what you need from our side (PO amendment, tax certificate, updated billing contact).

Attached: Cleardock_PO_4321.pdf

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Lee
Senior Procurement Manager | Cleardock
H: +44 20 5555 0123

--
Quoted-by: none

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@cleardock.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Aug 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request to change invoice payee & tax handling for PO 4321

Hi Hannah — thanks for the note and attaching the PO. Looping in Ben (sales ops) and Kim (finance/legal) to confirm process. Quick answers up front:

- We can route invoices to a different Redwood legal entity but it depends on whether the Order Form is tied to the US entity or if the customer-facing entity can be swapped via amendment.
- VAT reverse-charge treatment generally requires: (1) Cleardock EU VAT ID or valid tax cert, (2) invoice to the EU entity name and address, and (3) our finance team to map the Order Form to that EU bill-to entity.

Two options that are usually workable:
1) Minimal amendment: a one-page Order Form amendment that changes the invoice payee and billing address and references PO 4321. Quick and keeps commercial terms (pricing, min commit, net terms) identical.
2) Billing-entity migration: more involved — we create an Order Form amendment that also triggers entity mapping in our billing system. This can affect invoicing flows and potentially payment routing for upfront credits. If you need the EU entity to be the contract counterparty, that becomes a legal MSA consideration.

Ben/Kim — can you confirm the standard template we should use for option (1) and whether there are any implications for the minimum-commit allocation or net terms if we just swap the payee (i.e., does sales need to re-assign revenue to a different legal entity)?

Hannah — if you can share Cleardock EU VAT ID and the desired billing address, I’ll kick off the amendment draft. Also happy to set a 15-min call if that’s easier.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Head of Commercials | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0199

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Aug 2025 13:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request to change invoice payee & tax handling for PO 4321

Marcus / Kim — quick operational note from sales ops:

If we do the minimal amendment (option 1), we should explicitly call out that only the invoice payee and billing address change and that all commercial terms remain as-is (pricing schedule, minimum commit, net terms = Net 30). That avoids accidental reallocation of revenue. I suggest the amendment language: "Billing Payee: Redwood Inference (EMEA) S.à r.l. to be the invoice recipient for the Order Form referenced by PO 4321. All other commercial terms unchanged."

Action items for Cleardock to speed this up:
- Send EU VAT ID and the exact legal name + address to appear on invoices.
- Confirm if they want invoices sent to invoices-eu@cleardock.com or to payments@cleardock.com (the latter is copied).

I’ll draft the one-page amendment and a short billing mapping checklist. No change expected to the minimum commit math but we should note in the amendment that payments and service volume recognition remain governed by the original Order Form.

Ben
Ben Carter
Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@cleardock.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Sep 2025 15:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request to change invoice payee & tax handling for PO 4321

Hi Hannah — copying final steps so Cleardock has what you need to complete the change. We prepared a short amendment draft that only swaps the invoice payee and billing address and preserves all commercial terms (pricing schedule / minimum-commit / Net 30). We included a clause confirming tax treatment is per applicable law and that the customer certifies their VAT ID for reverse-charge.

I attached the draft amendment and a small tax evidence request (we only need your EU VAT ID and the billing contact email). Once you return those, we will:
1) Execute the amendment via DocuSign (link below).
2) Update our billing system and issue the first invoice to Cleardock Europe OU with reverse-charge notation.

Attachments: orderform_amendment_draft.docx; tax_certificate_request.docx

DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/sign/ABC123-cleardock-orderform

If Cleardock needs the EU entity to be the legal contracting party (not just invoice payee), let us know immediately as that requires a different MSA counterparty review and is not covered by this amendment.

Thanks — look forward to the VAT ID and billing email.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Finance & Legal Operations | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
